function: Multi-user CSI feedback: UE encoders compress angle-delay CSI and send it over a noisy uplink (DJSCC); a BS residual cross-attention transformer jointly reconstructs nearby users' CSI (pp. 2-3).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OFDM; BS ULA with Nt = 32 antennas serving single-antenna UEs (2 to 4 tested); 6.7 GHz; AWGN uplink; no RIS (pp. 1-3).
method: Transformer encoder/decoder with residual cross-attention blocks (RCA-MUNet), end-to-end MSE training with DJSCC; two-stage training: pretrain over SNRs, then fine-tune per SNR (p. 2).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa dataset per 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa, 6.7 GHz; 4 spatially correlated UEs within a 300 m x 300 m cell; 80,000/20,000/10,000 train/validation/test samples (p. 3).
test_conditions: Same QuaDRiGa UMa dataset for training and testing; sweeps over compression ratio, uplink SNR (pretrain 0-20 dB, fine-tune per SNR) and number of UEs, 2 to 4 (pp. 3-5).
baselines: BL1 single-user transformer (own variant); BL2 ADJSCC-CSINet+ [11]; BL3 multi-user fusion of [10]; BL4, BL5 ablations; CDL-OP dictionary learning [18]; SSCC with LDPC and QAM (pp. 3-5).
metrics: NMSE (dB) of CSI reconstruction versus compression ratio, uplink SNR and number of UEs; FLOPs and parameters (pp. 3-5).
complexity: FLOPs and parameters of BL1-BL3 and Ours in Table II: Ours 5.55 M parameters, 289.83 M FLOPs for 2 UEs, 579.66 M for 4 UEs (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 3: "in accordance with the 3GPP TR 38.901 [16]" - the CSI dataset is generated by QuaDRiGa in the UMa scenario at 6.7 GHz and used for training and testing.
q2_support: p. 3: "The downlink CSI dataset is generated by QuaDRiGa [17]" - one UMa 6.7 GHz dataset serves training and testing; only sweeps of SNR, compression ratio and number of UEs follow, and the paper never says that a model trained with 2 UEs is tested with 3 or 4 UEs.
q3_support: p. 3: "BL2 is the DJSCC-based single-user" CSI feedback of [11], and BL3 adds the fusion of [10] (earlier learned methods); p. 4: "significantly outperform the noise-free CDL-OP, revealing" - CDL-OP is the conventional dictionary-learning CS method of [18]; all compared in NMSE (Table I).
q4_support: p. 4: "operations (FLOPs) and parameters of BL1, BL2, BL3, and" - Table II reports FLOPs and parameters, with Ours at 5.55 M parameters and 289.83 M FLOPs for 2 UEs.
q5_support: p. 3: "The downlink CSI dataset is generated by QuaDRiGa [17]" - the authors generate their own simulated dataset; no code or data link or DOI is given, and no public or measured dataset is used.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match (Residual Cross-Attention Transformer-Based Multi-User CSI Feedback With DJSCC). Area 2. q3: the non-learned comparator CDL-OP [18] learns a dictionary offline, though the paper calls it a conventional CS-based approach (p. 4), so the reviewer should confirm; BL2 and BL3 are earlier learned methods, while BL1, BL4, BL5 and the SSCC scheme (same trained encoders) are variants and are not counted. q2: Fig. 3 extends the number of UEs to 3 and 4 but the paper does not state whether the model was trained with fewer UEs, so it is not counted.
